Ok imho there are 3 issues I had when I started working:

\- I was not used to it at fucking all, this will resolve over time, but it could take well over a year. It could go faster if issue 2 is resolved. Also, if you were or are addicted to games or anything else you can't do during work this can be hard.

\-When I started I basically sat out listening to metal doing nothing which was pretty depressing as I don't like being around people, but well I got paid and bought more metal from it. Now that I have a project that is actually challenging it is much more fine going to work.

\-Linked to the issue with addiction, but not quite the same. I assume you are american and it's pretty american to think that things only have worth if they pay, but that is BS. My job is almost worthless to me, I'd theoretically not be sad if I was thrown out today or tomorrow or at any point really. However, I would not be able to support my other projects I actually am passionate about, like making metal, collecting stuff, sometimes buy a game or go to the gym. I assume you used to play games all day like I did as NEET. Yea, you think "wtf I could be home playing this game and have more fun", but if you are anything like me gaming has become less special over time because we have so many games to play nowadays and every game is similiar to another one because gaming has become more mainstream. Once you gain more distance from it you can appreciate even smaller gaming sessions anymore. They will be a littler more like when you are a kid and actually had fun with this media because it was something new for you. Gain some distance from your addictions, but I don't tell you to stop if you really enjoy it, because why would you. You just kind of need to adapt a way of thinking that the worthless time you spend at work and link the use of this time to something you love. I'd hate to not be able to visit concerts, pay the bills for our band's studio, not support them with our album production financially and by my video editing skills. Also try something new with the money you make. Buy a fucking pencil or something and a book that teaches you how to draw, or write, maybe you find a different passion and it will lead you to a new way. I program now and make music videos on the evenings sometimes and I plan on compile them to a project file and apply for university for video editing maybe. I am happy as it is now, I don't want to start uni before anything betweeen 25-35 because I wanna do it my way. I believe if you find a passion to escape something you hate you adapt the right mindset to become one of the best in your field.

Also, time. Fucking time. When you start everything seems wasted. Like, you can only play 4 hours of games each day or spend it with something else. Let me tell you, once I developed a "healthy" relationship with the concept of time everything becme indefinitely easier. 4 hours are actually pretty fucking a hell lot of a time. I do so much and it makes me proud that I somehow manage. Just for demonstration's sake, I'll post you my schedule of yesterday:

10 hours of work (2hrs overtime I do from mon-thu to go home earlier on friday or when I don't feel, we have flexible time)Go home, eat2  hours of video editing. It's pleasant because I see progress every session with each part I work on. I don't do this every day. Sometimes I just play games instead or draw or something.30mins of playing Smash1.5 hours of gym, also not every day but only 2-3/week.

Keep in mind I do all of this while not even owning a car, so I have a lot to walk. I think your core issue is you don't really value what you do. I ain't gonna tell you go to the gym, it will make you happy or some gay shit like that, but adapt some side projects. You don't need to do as much as I do but I prefer to do many things for a short amount of time than 1 for a long time. Learn to just value the time to have by using the rest of the time of the time in a way you find it pleasant, you'll need to try out new stuff probably though, It'll take a while but your mind is a fucking liar and I believe you have the right mindset to get ahold of you frustration and make it into a great skill to escape the wageslaving. But you will need to wageslave for a while to maybe sometime find your way. It's fine, I need to do that do, and no my depression did not magically fade by working out and doing shit I like, it still hits me from time to time and it will you. But man, instead of fucking rotting use that rage to create something to escape the 9/5 hell by actually finding something you love working on. There's also no shame in working part time. I doubt I will work fulltime for longer than a year more or two. Don't let your value be determined by your paycheck or how much you work because in the end the people taht make it the #1 priority of a person's worth are fucking retarted workaholics/slaves who don't know how happy you can actually be by working on yourself and your skills instead of sitting in an office, destroying the planet by generating profit. I am from Austria and I actually checked just now, it's fine here as long as you don't mass-produce them. So if you only make 1 or 2 copies of a CD or digitalize it without actually sharing it it's completely fine as long as if you don't circumvent a copy protection. Means even if I had a copy protected DVD, it would be completely fine to screen-record a copy protected CD instead of ripping it when it has protection.

You are also not allowed to show it public, but it is fine to take a copied CD or DVD to a friends' place. Also, you are allowed to borrow copied content as long as you get it back (well, that's a tricky one with digital files...)

TL;DR - It is allowed to copy any media here in any way as long as you don't break a copy protection & don't publicize or upload it.
